notice: RN bank batch 154: Mental health case studies: autism in hospital, conduct disorder with fire-setting, antisocial personality disorder and factitious disorder imposed on another. questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues in autism spectrum disorder.

questions.stem: For each behavior, indicate the feature of autism spectrum disorder it shows.

rows.text: Little eye contact and literal understanding
Lines up toys and insists on the same route
Covers ears at the sound of a vacuum
Repeats phrases from a show (echolalia)
Eats only foods of one texture

rationale.correct: ASD involves social communication, repetitive behaviors and sensory differences.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The best approach is to {{b1}}, using {{b2}}.

options.text: keep routines as close to home as possible and reduce stimulation
change caregivers often so the child gets used to people
place the child near the nurses' station for noise
stop the rocking
the picture board, simple words and a visual schedule
long verbal explanations
sudden touch to get attention
sarcasm or jokes

rationale.correct: Routine, low stimulation and visual communication.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize care for a child with autism.

questions.stem: Which parts of the plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: A private, quiet room with dimmed lights
The same nurse each shift when possible
Bring familiar items such as a blanket and pasta from home
Show each step with pictures before it happens
Door alarm or close observation
Surprise the child with procedures to avoid anxiety

rationale.correct: Quiet room, consistency, familiar items, visual prep and safety.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

exhibits.title: Plan
exhibits.body: Child life specialist to prepare with a picture story. First case of the day.

questions.stem: Which actions help the surgery day go smoothly? Select all that apply.

options.text: Schedule as the first case to avoid waiting
Let the parent stay until the child is asleep
Share the child's triggers and calming strategies at every handoff
Ask the anesthesia team about premedication if needed
Ask the parent to leave early so the child adjusts
Use physical restraint as the first approach

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The immediate priority is {{b1}}, so the nurse should {{b2}}.

improving grades
family therapy only
teaching about cannabis
remove the lighter and search belongings per policy

exhibits.body: Lighter removed. Teen angry, threatens to burn the unit.

questions.stem: The teen shouts, "You can't make me follow your stupid rules!" Which responses are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: "Lights out is at 2200."
"You sound angry. We can talk."
"Following the plan earns phone time."
"You're acting like a criminal, just like your father."
"Fine, do whatever you want tonight; I give up arguing."

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize care for antisocial personality disorder.

questions.stem: Which parts of the plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Give opioids exactly as ordered and assess pain objectively
Tell the provider about the unprescribed benzodiazepines
Agree on a behavior contract with clear consequences
Monitor sedation and respiratory rate
Give an extra dose if the client threatens to complain
Withhold all pain medicine as punishment

rationale.correct: Treat pain safely, report the drug screen and set limits.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)

caseStudies.title: Child with autism spectrum disorder in hospital

exhibits.title: Admission
exhibits.body: A 7-year-old child with autism spectrum disorder is admitted for dental surgery under anesthesia. The child speaks in short phrases, covers the ears at loud sounds and eats only plain pasta. The parent says, "He melts down when his routine changes."

rows.label: Sensory
cells: Distressed by bright lights and beeping alarms

rows.label: Behavior
cells: Rocks and flaps hands when anxious

rows.label: Routine
cells: Bath, story and bed at 1930 every night

rows.label: Safety
cells: Has wandered away from home twice

exhibits.title: Admission
exhibits.body: A 14-year-old was admitted after setting a fire in a school trash can. Over a year the teen has set small fires, stolen from stores, skipped school and hurt the family dog. The teen says, "It's not a big deal."

rows.label: On the unit
cells: Took a lighter from a visitor's bag

caseStudies.title: Antisocial personality disorder on a medical unit

exhibits.title: Medical unit
exhibits.body: A 35-year-old client admitted with a leg wound infection has a history of assault and fraud. The client is charming to some staff, demands extra opioids, and tells a new nurse, "The other nurse lets me have two doses. You're my favorite, you'll help me." The client has been seen in another client's room.

rows.label: Pain
cells: Rates 10/10 while laughing on the phone

caseStudies.title: Factitious disorder imposed on a child

exhibits.title: Pediatric unit
exhibits.body: A 4-year-old child has had 11 admissions this year for vomiting and 'seizures' that no one but the parent has seen. Tests are always normal. The parent, a former nursing assistant, is very attentive, knows medical terms well and enjoys the staff's attention. Symptoms stop when the parent is away.

rows.label: Vomiting
cells: Only when the parent is present

rows.label: Siblings
cells: One sibling died in infancy of unexplained causes

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
